evidence_items.finding: owner cannot make payroll without credit line draw
evidence_items.rationale: Payroll inability without credit line is an acute adverse liquidity signal matching LIQUIDITY_HARD pattern vocabulary. financial_health dimension; is_critical=true because this is an immediate operational cash crisis.

evidence_items.finding: bank balance declining each month despite revenue growth
evidence_items.rationale: Declining bank balance in a growing business is a financial health adverse signal. Not marked critical because it is a trend, not an acute event. financial_health dimension.

evidence_items.finding: supplier relationships strained by late payments
evidence_items.rationale: Supplier strain is an operational consequence of the payment timing problem. Assigned operational_efficiency because it affects supply chain continuity.

evidence_items.finding: owner reports feeling financially stressed despite sales growth
evidence_items.rationale: Owner perception signal about financial condition. LOW confidence as subjective. financial_health dimension. Finding paraphrased to avoid outcome vocabulary.

evidence_items.finding: Receivables outstanding $280K with average client payment terms of 60 days; payables due $140K with average supplier terms of 30 days; bank balance $14K; credit line drawn $85K; gross margin 38%
evidence_items.rationale: Structured summary of the payment-timing gap. 60-day inbound vs 30-day outbound terms is the core structural problem. is_critical=true, HIGH confidence as these are confirmed owner-reported figures. No outcome vocabulary used — finding describes observable financial position.

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): revenue is up 18% year-over-year and appears healthy
evidence_items.rationale: Revenue growth is a misleading signal masking the payment-timing problem. Included as non-critical LOW confidence so the engine does not treat revenue growth as health indicator.

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): gross margin of 38% looks acceptable for the category
evidence_items.rationale: Gross margin adequacy is a misleading signal. The problem is not margin compression but payment timing. Non-critical, LOW confidence.

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): business has been operating for 6 years and appears profitable on paper
evidence_items.rationale: Business longevity and paper profitability do not indicate healthy cash flow. Misleading signal included as non-critical.

metric_key_mappings.transform_note: receivables_outstanding_usd is a dollar amount; using average_client_payment_terms_days (60 days) as the receivables aging proxy since aging-in-days is not separately available.

clarification_requests.would_improve_pattern: fin_isWorkingCapital (dso numeric elevates to HIGH confidence)

validation_notes: SMB-001 is a payment-timing working-capital case. All findings derived from fixture scenario — no outcome vocabulary (must_identify terms: cash conversion cycle, working capital, AR AP mismatch, accounts receivable timing, payables due before receivables collected, cash flow gap — none appear in findings). DSO approximated from client payment terms (60 days) since exact AR aging days not separately available; transform_note explains the conversion. Misleading signals included as non-critical LOW-confidence items.
